flagship_directive: Resolve oeq:finite-profile-certification by constructing a terminating finite-profile approximation whose endpoint enclosures have uniformly certified deterministic error o(r_n), thereby converting the exact-profile existence band into a reproducible rate-preserving procedure.
critique: The note proves a two-sided minimax expected-maximal-width rate over the stated law class, with the upper bound supplied by measurable extrema of an exact infinite-dimensional profile and the converse supplied by a fixed-nuisance Bernoulli marked pair. It does not prove a terminating procedure for computing or finitely certifying those extrema to o(r_n) accuracy, so the delivered band is an existence theorem rather than an implementable inference method. Accordingly, the consumer claim about translating the frontier into study-design calculations exceeds the supplied evidence because neither computable endpoints nor finite-sample constants are provided. The TL;DR and scope sections otherwise describe the matched statistical frontier accurately and explicitly leave only finite-profile certification open; this computational and practical-evidence gap, rather than an unmatched theorem, is the main constraint on the projected paper score.
